thread:
alex: Morning—quick recap from overnight. We had two 5xx spikes between 02:10-02:40 UTC causing elevated tail latency for hosted/text-gen. Root cause was an autoscaler anomaly + one pod stuck in CrashLoopBackoff. Customer impact: intermittent 5–10% error rate for ~30m to a subset of requests routed to that AZ.

ops-bot: INCIDENT: pagerduty#P12345 triggered by gateway (5xx spike). Severity: Sev2. Notes: automatic rollback to model-variant 'gptx-quant-lite' was attempted and failed for 3 requests.

ajie: @alex thanks. do we have the pod logs? any OOM or oom_kill?

alex: logs show repeated kernel OOM killer messages on that node, memory pressure on CUDA driver, then kubelet restart attempt. snippet:```
OOMKILL: process=triton_server pid=4821 rss=13.2G
kubelet: evicting pods, memory.available < 300MB
```

jamie: I restarted the node pool autoscaler group briefly (target +1) which let the scheduler put new pods up. After that error rate dropped to baseline around 02:45. Confirmed with tracing that latency percentiles recovered.

priya: TL;DR for the handoff: incident stabilized, autoscaler worked around the stuck pod, no rollback required. No customer-facing notification sent, but a few internal monitors fired.

lia: Good. Two gaps to highlight for next shift: 1) we don't have an explicit runbook step for 'node-level GPU memory pressure' that cross-references driver restart vs. pod eviction. 2) our alert thresholds for sustained 5xx per-AZ are slightly permissive — they aggregated across regions which delayed page by ~4m.

alex: Agree. Action items I did: opened a short PR to add a runbook section (link below) and bumped the per-AZ 5xx alert to trigger at 1.5% sustained over 2m. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/642

alex: Runbook we referenced: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/infra/gpu-memory-pressure (draft). Add to your review queue @lia @jamie.

jamie: For next 12h coverage: I'm primary from 08:00–20:00 UTC, @priya is secondary until 16:00 UTC then @alex takes over (per rotation). There's a 2-hour overlap gap from 06:00–08:00 UTC tomorrow where no one is listed as secondary — we should decide.

priya: I can cover that gap tomorrow morning (06:00–08:00 UTC) if needed. I'll update the rotation spreadsheet and ping on call-ops channel.

lia: Please do. Also add a short run-through in the morning scrum at 07:30 so the inbound secondary knows the recent flakiness.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: model-service/v2 rolled out at 2026-05-05T02:00Z. Canary passed 01:58Z. No rollout-related anomalies recorded.

alex: Notes for whoever picks this up: if you see a per-AZ 5xx spike, checklist:
1) check node memory metrics: `node_memory_usable_bytes` and GPU driver logs
2) check pod restarts: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running`
3) if device driver is unstable, cordon node and trigger replacement: `kubectl cordon <node>` then remove from autoscaler group.
4) if sustained customer impact >10m, escalate to infra and notify on #status (we didn't need to for this one).

jamie: Follow-ups:
- @lia: write the explicit driver vs eviction decision tree in runbook (owner)
- @priya: update rotation sheet, cover 06:00–08:00 gap (owner)
- @alex: revert alert tweak if we see noisy firing for small blips (owner)

priya: I'll file a short post-incident note in the incidents channel and include the trace links + customer sampling IDs.

lia: Suggest we add a small synthetic test hitting the hosted/text-gen route through that AZ every 5m for added early detection. I'll file a ticket.

alex: Closing remarks: system is stable, no customer escalations. Primary/secondary for next rotation: jamie (primary 08:00–20:00), priya (secondary until 16:00), alex (backup after 16:00). Please ack.

jamie: ack.

priya: ack.

lia: ack.

ops-bot: THREAD NOTE: archived in 7d per retention policy.
